page: The Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1920s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity is provisioned at 64.0 GB RAM, which establishes an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. High-speed local persistence is supplied by an integrated 1920 GB NVMe SSD. No dedicated GPUs are included, and one complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned to the virtual machine.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent compute and throughput capabilities across standard enterprise tasks. The CPU achieves a top-tier stress-ng single-core score of 3138.07, alongside an average multi-core score of 25024.21 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 7990.0. Memory subsystems sustain 117.28 GB/sec in large-block uncached sequential reads and 69.27 GB/sec in writes. Synthetic database operations reach 3656.13 on PassMark, while in-memory caching yields 15.09 million Redis SET operations per second.

Because the configuration couples an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation with substantial local NVMe capacity, the resource balance favors data-intensive workloads over raw compute scale. The lack of AVX-512 instruction extensions limits intensive vector processing and large model prompt ingestion, as evidenced by lower prompt processing throughput on 7B LLM tests. However, dedicated CPU cores and large local storage deliver reliable, non-burstable operational profiles without shared-tenant interference.

The voc-s-8c-64gb-1920s-amd is well-matched for intermediate database deployments, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, CI/CD artifact handling, ETL pipelines, and high-throughput static web hosting requiring direct high-speed disk access.
